title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1970 work on crystalline Dieudonné theory for Barsotti–Tate groups and their truncations (ICM Nice 1970; Montréal lectures, published 1974). The page is written on the back of a typescript complex-analysis course; the neighbouring pages are unrelated scrap.

(1) Top. A distinguished triangle ℓ → Δ → ℓ̌'[1] → in D(X). Here ℓ is a co-Lie complex (cohomology ω, n), Δ is the Dieudonné crystal evaluated on X (written D*(G)), and ℓ̌' is the dual of the co-Lie complex of the dual group. This is the 'Hodge filtration' of the Dieudonné crystal in derived form: Fil^0Δ = Δ, Fil^1Δ = ℓ, Fil^2Δ = 0.

(2) Comparison triangle. It is compared with the trivially filtered object 0 → θ ≅ θ → 0, with Fil^0θ = θ and Fil^1θ = 0. A filtered map Δ → θ sending ℓ to 0 is, 'i.e.', a map ℓ̌'[1] → θ. In a triangulated category such a factorisation exists but is not unique. Hence the marginal note 'modulo les diff. ...', apparently about homotopy or ambiguity: the factorisations form a torsor under the image of Hom(ℓ[1], θ).

(3) Restriction question. Grothendieck then looks at the restriction square Hom_{D(X)}(ℓ̌'[1], θ) → Hom(Δ, θ), and its image under φ* in Hom_{D(X_cris)}(φ*ℓ̌'[1], φ*θ). The question is whether a map defined on the Zariski/étale side and compatible with the filtration is determined by, or comes from, crystalline data. With θ = O_X[1] these Hom groups become H^0's: H^0(ℓ') → H^0(Δ̌*), with a vertical arrow to H^0(φ*ℓ'). The same is done for the dual triangle ℓ → Δ̌* → ℓ̌[1].

(4) Six-term sequence. Taking cohomology gives
0 → n_{G*} → D*(G)^∨ → t_G → ω_{G*} → D*(G*) → γ_G → 0,
matched with H^1(ℓ') → H^1(Δ') → H^1(ℓ̌[-1]) → H^0(ℓ') → H^0(Δ') → H^0(ℓ̌[1]) → 0. This is the derived Hodge sequence for a finite flat (truncated BT) group, where ℓ_G has two cohomology sheaves, ω and n. In the BT case it would collapse to 0 → ω → D → t → 0.

(5) Bottom. Grothendieck splits off 0 → n_{G*} → D*(G)^∨ → Q → 0 and considers Γ(D*(G*)) → Γ(t_G) → H^0(ℓ') and H^1(n_{G*}) → H^1_cris(n_{G*}). He then records a conjunction of conditions: H^1(D*(G)^∨) = 0 and Ker(H^1(n_{G*}) → H^1_cris(n_{G*})) ≠ 0. This reads as a test situation, a sketch of a counterexample or obstruction. A class in H^1(n_{G*}) that dies crystallinely would make the Zariski-side map (or factorisation) non-unique or non-liftable, while the vanishing of H^1(D^∨) controls the crystalline side.

Purpose: to see whether the Hodge-filtration triangle for truncated BT groups, and maps out of it, are canonically determined by the Dieudonné crystal (functoriality and uniqueness of the triangle), or whether there is an obstruction in H^1(n).
errors: No outright errors are visible. The central identification 'Δ→θ with ℓ→0, i.e. ℓ̌'[1]→θ' only holds up to the ambiguity Hom(ℓ[1],θ). Grothendieck flags this himself in the marginal 'modulo' note, so it is a recognised gap rather than a mistake.

The final pair of conditions is stated without any construction of an example. It is unclear whether such G exists, so the intended conclusion (non-uniqueness or non-functoriality) is left unproven on the page.

ideas.modern_name: Hodge filtration of Dieudonné crystal for truncated Barsotti–Tate groups (co-Lie complex version)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a test for whether the derived Hodge-filtration triangle of a truncated BT group is canonically determined by the crystal. He reduces it to the conditions H^1(D^∨)=0 together with a nonzero kernel of H^1(n_{G*})→H^1_cris(n_{G*}). No example is constructed. The canonicity/functoriality of this triangle was later handled (via the co-Lie complex) by Illusie and by BBM, so the thread is largely absorbed by the literature. Only the specific obstruction formulation looks unrecorded.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A minor historical detail: it shows Grothendieck explicitly worrying about the non-uniqueness of the Hodge triangle for non-BT groups in 1970. This issue resurfaces in modern derived and prismatic treatments of Dieudonné theory for finite flat groups (e.g. Anschütz–Le Bras). It is unlikely to be mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: These are fragmentary working notes on the Hodge filtration of Dieudonné crystals for truncated BT groups, a topic Grothendieck announced in 1970 and that Illusie and BBM later developed. The obstruction test is a nice glimpse of his thinking but is unfinished and is subsumed by later work.
transcription_corrections: 'H^1(ℓ̌(-1))' and 'H^0(ℓ̌(1))' should read H^1(ℓ̌[-1]) and H^0(ℓ̌[1]) (shift brackets).
The marginal note reads roughly 'modulo les diff. d'h[omotopie?] ... la comparaison[?] ...'; it is partly illegible.
In the line H^0(ℓ·) → H^0(Δ̌*), the target is a corrected Δ with superscript ∨*. The crossed-out item beside the vertical arrow is a struck '→ H^{-1}(ℓ')'.
The top-left mark is a crossed-out symbol, not part of the triangle.
The previous and next pages are unrelated typescript (a complex-analysis course) used as scrap paper; this page has archive number 21.
